title: Test a paged reader through exhaustion, not just its first batch
applies_when: A file, archive or adapter exposes repeated bounded reads on one handle, with a contract to advance through entries and eventually report exhaustion. A first full-directory listing can pass while the paged protocol is broken.
lesson: Check the state transition across calls. In Afero zipfs at eb6a928, Readdir and Readdirnames each restart traversal of the same map; bounded callers repeat entries and never reach EOF. Use a finite fixture and bounded call sequence, collecting every entry once, then repeat exhausted reads. Cover partial final batches, zero/negative counts after a bounded read, mixed metadata/name methods sharing one cursor, empty directories, independent handles and Close. Do not require a particular map order. A per-handle entry snapshot plus offset provides stable traversal; compare counts against remaining entries before adding them to the offset to avoid huge-count overflow. Release retained snapshot state on Close. Filter adapters have a different failure: consuming one underlying batch does not establish visible progress. Afero RegexpFile can return empty+nil on a positive read after filtering, panic on a nil passthrough filter, and discard entries returned with an error. Read only the remaining requested count until visible entries satisfy the count or an error occurs; preserve entries and the original error together through name conversion. Test rejecting/matching/nil filters on real memory and OS backends, mixed methods and partial EOF/error results. This streaming repair needs no snapshot. Run identical regressions on unchanged and repaired production; a baseline compile failure from asserting a new private field is setup failure, not bug discrimination.
avoid_when: A stateless listing API may deliberately restart, or require an explicit continuation token rather than a file cursor. Check that contract first. Snapshotting adds O(directory entry count) metadata and does not justify sorting or buffering archive contents. ZIP evidence includes Linux Go1.26.9 root-module race/vet and native Windows/amd64 CGO-disabled ZIP tests. RegexpFile evidence includes Linux root-module race/vet only; Windows binaries compiled but application control denied execution, which must not be bypassed. Neither covers all platforms, Go versions, concurrent handle use or cloud modules. Existing first-listing/path controls do not prove pagination, and a separate failure does not invalidate those controls. Repairing RegexpFile does not repair an outer IOFS adapter dropping partial results; that is separately covered by PR667. An open PR is not maintainer acceptance, portable performance or measured Scout-routing benefit.

evidence.note: Pinned baseline: both directory methods rebuild their result from map traversal with no directory cursor or exhausted positive-read EOF.

Common public-API regressions and controls cover the sequence and resource lifetime. The repaired source was independently executed; no private-field assertion is needed to compile the tests on the baseline.
Proposed shared-cursor repair with explicit memory and validation scope; Linux and native Windows matched checks pass after baseline assertion failures. This is not a merge or performance claim.

Exact repaired production path: filtered reads refill the remaining visible count and preserve data with errors. This affinity link makes the scoped advice discoverable when Scout reads RegexpFile, without fetching more source. Retrieval is not measured model use or yield.

Identical public-API tests on unchanged eb6a928 fail20/pass10 test/subtest events; repaired RegexpFile passes30. Linux root-module race passes249/one existing platform skip, vet passes. No Windows execution or performance claim.

Independent streaming filtered-read repair; positive reads refill after rejected entries, nil filters pass through, and data plus errors survive name conversion. No ZIP snapshot or outer IOFS changes.
